subtitle: A private 1870s tunnel through Caversham Sandstone, hand-carved by a politician for beach access and reopened to the public in 1983.
spike_statement: Politician John Cargill hand-carved this tunnel in the 1870s for private beach access; the drowned-daughters legend attached to it is fiction.

levers.photo_tone: Ochre Caversham Sandstone cliffs and a shadowed tunnel mouth against grey Southern Ocean swell, cut through by a single shaft of daylight.
